summary:
This lecture explains the Islamic practice of wiping over footwear (khuffs) during ablution (wudu), a topic that is often misunderstood. The speaker emphasizes the importance of approaching acts of worship with the best effort rather than doing only the bare minimum required. He details the Prophet Muhammad's method of wiping over footwear: making complete wudu, putting on socks or shoes, then wiping over the tops of the feet once with wet hands during subsequent ablutions. The speaker clarifies that this practice is valid for 24 hours for residents and 72 hours for travelers, counting from the first time one wipes over the footwear.

The lecture addresses common misconceptions and practical questions about wiping over footwear. Key points include that the material of the footwear is irrelevant—what matters is that it covers the area that would normally be washed and is difficult to remove. The speaker explains that merely taking off the footwear does not break one's wudu, but one can only wipe over footwear if they were put on after performing wudu with washed feet. The only reasons to remove the footwear are if ghusl (full body ritual washing) is required or if the 24-48 hour time limit has expired.
